title: True labor, self-knowledge, and the soul's nobility
english: A lover of labor is the one who has time in abundance. Do not accept the outward appearance of a Christian man, but the mind of his soul. To blame the blameless one is sin against God. Great is the danger of ears and tongue.

It is absurd for one who pursues honors to flee the labors through which honors come. Do you wish to know God? First know yourself. A true friend is one who shares in adversities. It is terrible to think highly of oneself while doing small ones. In everything, supposing hinders knowing. A demon is the guide of a life without reason. The nobility of the soul is revealed by its vigor. God-fearing is the one who does not speak on his own authority. A blameless person is a temple of God. A worthless life is the worst possession. Say what you ought and when you ought, and you will not hear what you ought not. A friend who never fails is the greatest possession. A vainglorious disposition is a disease of the soul. A stranger and a poor man is God's eye-salve—the one who receives him will quickly see again.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: The speaker is the treatise's unnamed teacher, continuing a series of alphabetically arranged spiritual maxims; this section runs from phi through omicron and then begins a new alphabetic series from alpha.

title: Virtue, friendship, and the soul's ascent
english: It is good to benefit everyone, but especially those who cannot repay. An orator in righteousness is a cup of cold water. Self-control and gentleness of soul are cherubim. To be honored in old age is proof of having been industrious before old age; earnestness in a young man is a guarantee that he will be honored in old age. The upper room of the soul is true contemplation. If you love what you ought not, you will not love what you ought. It is better to possess counterfeit gold than a counterfeit friend. A pure soul after God is a god. Alas for the self-love that hates all things!

The beginning of love is an opinion of glory. It is good to be rich in gentleness and love. A proud thought is the winnower of virtue. The road becomes smooth through almsgiving. An unjust judge is a defiled conscience. It is terrible to be enslaved to the passions of the flesh. If you wish to be without grief, strive to please God. The one who cares well for himself is cared for by God. A self-controlled heart is a harbor of contemplations.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: The speaker continues the alphabetical collection of spiritual maxims, now moving through sayings on benefaction, self-control, friendship, and the soul's relation to God.

title: Self-knowledge, humility, and life in Christ
english: When you want to know who you are, do not measure yourself against who you were. Consider what you have become from the beginning. A soul full of vainglory is a dry cistern. A soul full of pride is an inn for robbers, and it hates the sound of knowledge. For a true man, not to know the Scriptures is a grievous error. If you fear God, you will know it by your tears.

The humility of the soul is an unbreakable weapon. A man who loves virtue is a tree of paradise. Jesus Christ is the tree of life. Use him as you ought, and you will never die. Help those who are truly poor, and you will eat Christ. True strength is to eat the body of Christ.

If you love Christ, you will not forget to keep his commandments. For it is from there that a benefactor after God appears. A friend according to God flows with milk and honey with true words, but a lazy soul will have no such friend. A thought that loves pleasure is a cruel master. To keep silent about the truth is to bury gold. Whoever fears God does everything according to God.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: These closing sayings continue the alphabetical maxims on purifying the soul from passions and attaining union with Christ by keeping his commandments.
